compiler.rationale: .github/workflows/aiken-ci.yml pins exactly one compiler for compilation, for every applied validator hash and for executing the test suite: the patched fork built from Anastasia-Labs/aiken rev 2a78108ccb184161689b8a06c84d942e13b5b209 (tag midgard-2a78108c), whose AIKEN_FORK_VERSION is `aiken v1.1.23+2a78108`. Stock v1.1.22 was retired from every role because the build that used to hold the compilation role ships a live unsound-codegen defect. The identity is therefore measured by spawning the resolved binary and is required to match the pin EXACTLY, not by prefix: a second fork build of the same 1.1.23 base reports a different `+<rev>` suffix and would supply this family's on-chain result under a compiler the tree does not pin.

output1RuleAndViolationIdentifier.rule: A block is invalid if two distinct transactions committed by its `transactions_root` spend the same UTxO. `tx1_id != tx2_id` plus an equal spent out-ref is the decisive pair; the on-chain family proves exactly that.

localEnforcement.note: Both sites are the same rule on the two candidate-application paths: a spent out-ref already consumed by an accepted transaction of the same block is rejected before the input is resolved.

catalogueBinding.note: The append-only id is the positional index encoded big-endian over FRAUD_PROOF_CATALOGUE_ID_BYTE_COUNT bytes, so index 0 is the 8-hex-digit id 00000000. The index is re-derived from the order constant rather than trusted, because inserting a category rather than appending one would silently re-number every family after it.

registeredFamiliesSuiteNotCited.reason: The registered-families lifecycle suite carries three lifecycles — no-reference-input, reference-input-no-idx and invalid-signature — and no double-spend lifecycle at all. It is therefore deliberately NOT cited for this family, and the absence is measured rather than assumed: the verifier requires the suite source to contain no `doubleSpend` occurrence, so a future double-spend lifecycle added there fails this gate until it is cited. Q10's catalogue-reachability passage is carried instead by the output-9 emulator journey, which asserts the computation-thread asset name against the deployed catalogue's `doubleSpend` category id.

output2SchemaAndCodecAgreement.claim: The evidence record a double-spend step consumes has one shape on both sides of the boundary: `NativeTxInclusionArgs` is field-for-field identical, in the same positional order, in the Aiken type and the SDK codec.
output2SchemaAndCodecAgreement.parityNote: Both field lists are parsed out of their own source file by the verifier and compared to each other and to this list. Positional agreement is what matters: these records reach the chain as Plutus data, so a re-ordered pair of same-typed fields is a silent mis-binding that no type checker on either side would catch. The shared binding itself is Q00/Q01-owned and is consumed, not edited, by this family.

output3FlatFieldHashBinding.boundFieldNote: Field 0 is the field this family opens. output4OnchainSelectors.claim: Every deployed step of the family carries at least one positive selector and at least one valid-block negative selector, and all of them are measured passing in one batched run under the pinned fork compiler.
output4OnchainSelectors.selectionNote: `aiken check -m <module>.{<test>}` names exactly one test, so the batch is exact: the run must collect precisely the declared selectors and no others. `aiken check` exits 0 on a selector that matches nothing, so a zero-collection or partial-collection run has to be failed by the derivation rather than by the exit code. selectors.claim: The first conflicting transaction is genuinely committed under the block's counted `transactions_root`, so its verified id reaches step-02.
The same binding through a 22-level membership proof carried by published chunks — the carriage route added at issue #545, past the direct route's envelope ceiling.
Published chunks stay bound to the header's counted transactions root; a forged root cannot bind.
The step is bound to the exact claim its redeemer named, so a merkelized verifier invoked on a different chunk order proves nothing this step asked for.

A transaction fabricated against a VALID block's header cannot bind: the raw transactions root is not the one that header's counted `transactions_root` commits, so the challenge dies before any conflict is claimed.
The second conflicting transaction is committed under the same counted root and is a different transaction from the one step-01 bound, so both verified ids reach step-03.
The same second binding through a 22-level published-chunk membership proof, with the distinctness argument unchanged.

A valid block never holds two distinct transactions spending one UTxO, so the only conflict assemblable against it is the same committed transaction named twice; the `tx1_id != tx2_id` check rejects it.
The carried preimage is the one tx1's field-0 commitment authenticates, so the selected input reaches step-04 alongside the untouched second transaction id.

Distinct transactions of a valid block spend disjoint inputs, so a conflict can only be manufactured by carrying a preimage that is not the bound transaction's; the door's authenticate-once hash check rejects it.
The compact structures must be the thread's transaction's: another committed transaction's compact CBOR fails the tx-id re-derivation before the door is reached.
Spec section 7 item 3, abort-never-clamp: an index past the committed collection fails the read instead of returning the nearest item.
The second transaction's authenticated field-0 preimage contains the same input carried from step-03, so the conflict is proven and the proof finalizes into a permanent fraud-proof token.
In a valid block the two transactions spend disjoint inputs, so the input carried from step-03 is not the one at the named index of tx2's authenticated preimage and the challenge cannot finalize.
The preimage must be tx2's own: substituting one that happens to contain the carried input fails the door's authenticate-once hash check.

delegatedOutputs.rationale: Outputs 5 to 8 are not unowned and are not re-derived here. They are bound family-locally for Q10 inside the SHARED four-family artifact, whose own gate is the executable authority for those cells and runs in the same battery as this one. That gate spawns five Vitest suites, including three emulator suites that drive the complete correction path at forced branch level 22 and at the admissible 296-input Cardano spend shape. Re-running them from this gate would double the battery's cost and would measure nothing the shared gate does not already measure. So this gate delegates the passage and asserts the delegation instead: it re-reads the shared artifact's Q10 cells for outputs 5 to 9, requires each to be LOCAL_PASS with no open cell left anywhere in that artifact, requires Q10 to appear in BOTH carriage remediations' measured-family lists, and then re-checks in this tree that the concrete Q10 surfaces those cells describe still exist and are still wired.
